B1.goal: Follow key events, supporting details and a speaker's main message.

gist.title: Which idea best summarises the speech?
options: Success comes from talent and hard work alone.
Success comes from effort, help and belonging.
Success means winning awards and being famous.
gist.why: He gives credit to other people and talks about belonging.

gist.title: Which description fits his tone?
options: Warm and sometimes funny
Angry and often critical
Cold and very formal
gist.why: He makes jokes, but he is also moved and grateful.

detail.title: Why does he joke about the lifetime award?
options: He says he is only halfway through his career.
He says he is planning to stop acting soon.
He says he did not want to come tonight.
detail.why: He is still a working actor.

detail.title: What happened in his third year at college?
options: He met people who were making a short film.
He joined a group of students who played in a band.
He found a group of people putting on plays.
detail.why: He felt lost and alone, then found people putting on plays.

detail.title: What does he say about entertainment and art?
options: He says he prefers making art to making entertainment.
Actors sometimes make entertainment and sometimes art.
He says most films today are entertainment, not art.
detail.why: "Sometimes we make entertainment. Sometimes we make art" - and if they are lucky, both at once.

C1.goal: Interpret subtext, rhetorical choices and nuanced attitudes to success.

gist.title: What broader claim links the personal stories?
options: A successful career is ultimately the result of individual talent and persistence.
An individual career can be understood through community and shared creative work.
Public recognition finally compensates for years of insecurity and rejection.
gist.why: His memories build a collaborative rather than individualistic view.

gist.title: How does the opening humour function?
options: It softens self-praise and builds rapport.
It signals irritation with the ceremony.
It distances him from the nominees present.
gist.why: The jokes acknowledge the honour without sounding self-important.

detail.title: His joke about receiving the award at the "half point" of his career mainly implies that ...
options: he remains committed to working
he is dissatisfied with his career so far
he objects to honours based on age
detail.why: "I'm still a working actor" - the exaggeration underlines continuing motivation.

detail.title: His account of college emphasises the transition from ...
options: alienation to belonging
poverty to financial security
acting to directing
detail.why: He moves from feeling lost and isolated to finding "my people".

detail.title: What follows from his idea that success brings freedom?
options: Greater status frees people from obligations.
Success is a private matter, not a public one.
Freedom comes with responsibility to help others.
detail.why: "A certain freedom that comes with responsibility" - to support others and keep the door open.

sequence: He opens with a joke about the award.
He looks back on his early career.
He names people from his past.
He tells a story from his college years.

facts.title: Name the two directors he thanks.

open.title: Explain how the jokes about the award contribute to Ford's ethos.
open.answer: The self-deprecating humour presents him as modest, approachable and still active.
open.criteria: Analyse a rhetorical effect with one concrete example.

C2.goal: Analyse rhetoric, implicit assumptions, narrative architecture and competing interpretations.

gist.title: Which reading best captures the speech's central tension?
options: He accepts the honour but suggests lifetime awards should be abolished.
He accepts a personal honour while redistributing credit to those behind his career.
He presents his long career as the product of his own talent, discipline and persistence alone.
gist.why: The speech both accepts an individual honour and redistributes credit.

gist.title: His treatment of fame is best described as ...
options: a repositioning of fame within collaboration and belonging
a wholesale rejection of popular success and celebrity
a claim that stardom remains the only truly meaningful reward for an actor's work
gist.why: He values work and connection over the myth of solitary triumph.

detail.title: What is the main effect of calling the honour "a prize for being alive"?
options: It openly questions whether lifetime achievement awards should exist at all.
It signals that he plans to retire soon and is looking back on a career he considers finished.
It is self-deprecating: he contrasts himself with nominees honoured for specific work.
detail.why: Nominees are there for their work; he gets "a prize for being alive". He then adds that it is "a little early" for a working actor.

detail.title: The college anecdote is structurally important because it ...
options: shows that formal education played no role at all in his eventual success as a professional actor
serves mainly as a humorous digression before the serious thanks
links the autobiographical past to the later call to welcome newcomers
detail.why: The outsider who found "my people" later asks others to keep the door open.

detail.title: What reading most closely follows his remarks about freedom?
options: Career autonomy matters more than obligations to others.
Artistic freedom and public responsibility are incompatible.
Influence should be matched by active support for others.
detail.why: Success brings "a certain freedom that comes with responsibility".

sequence: He opens with a joke about the occasion.
He turns to the early years of his career.
He names figures from his professional past.
He recounts an episode from his college years.

facts.title: Name the two filmmakers acknowledged after the career-struggle passage.

open.title: To what extent is the persona Ford presents in this speech itself carefully constructed?
open.answer: The speech resists heroic individualism through humour and gratitude, although even humility can help construct star charisma.
open.criteria: Offer both a reading and a counter-reading, grounded in two moments.
